title: Word Search II
summary: Find every word from a list that can be traced through adjacent cells of a letter grid.

tests.explain: Each found word is a chain of side-by-side cells, such as c → o → d → e for "code". "tend" and "card" would need a diagonal last step, and "rot" fails because the only o has no t next to it.
"abcd" would need c right after b, but those two cells only touch diagonally.
"aa" would need the single cell twice: a cell can be used only once per word.

hints: Searching the grid once per word repeats the same work for words that share a prefix. Can a single DFS check all the words at once?
Put the words in a trie. Start a DFS from every cell and move a trie pointer with it: if the next letter has no child in the trie, abandon this path.
Store each word on its end node; when the DFS reaches it, record the word and clear it so it is reported once. Mark a cell as used while it is on the current path and restore it when you backtrack.

complexity.time: O(m · n · 4 · 3^(L-1)) in the worst case for words up to length L, though the trie cuts most paths short; building the trie is O(total letters)
complexity.space: O(total letters) for the trie, plus O(L) recursion
